newsitem.title: JAPAN: Excessive yen weakness, strength undesirable - MITI.
newsitem.headline: Excessive yen weakness, strength undesirable - MITI.

text.p: Excessive weakness or strength in the yen is undesirable, Japan's Trade Minister Shinji Sato told a news conference on Tuesday.
"Both excessive weakness and excessive strength in the yen are undesirable," he said in reply to a question about the recent weakening of the yen against the dollar.
He also said that it was important for foreign exchange movements to be stable and that he would be watching the effects of currency movements on Japanese industry.
He also said that stable exchange rates will help balance Japan's trade with other countries.
Asked if it was necessary to do anything about the yen's weakening, Sato said, "We can't do anything without looking at (further) foreign exchange movements."

"There are both temporary and seasonal factors affecting currencies and and we will have to see for a while. Just because the dollar rises by one yen, it does not mean we have to do anything," he said.
